evidence: app/package.json:6-11 — dependencies are exactly nuxt 4.6.3, vue 3.5, vue-router 4.5, all current stable
app/nuxt.config.ts:1-21 — only stable config options (compatibilityDate, devtools, css, app.head, runtimeConfig); no experimental flags
app/app/pages/pokemon/[name].vue:4 — setResponseStatus imported from h3 v1 (1.15.11 per package-lock.json:4644-4645), the long-stable server API
app/app/pages/index.vue:14 — useAsyncData with the stable `watch`/query options, APIs stable since Nuxt 3
reach.rationale: The app sits entirely on long-stable APIs of the current stable Nuxt release (4.6.3, published 2026-10-27); measured experimental markers are empty and grep for experimental/unstable/preview found nothing.

evidence: app/app/lib/pokeapi.ts:1-60 — all API access funneled through one hand-rolled module (api(), cache, limited()), no experimental data-fetching features
app/app/composables/useApiBase.ts:1-9 — the single place env/config is resolved, wrapping stable useState/useRuntimeConfig
app/app/pages/[...slug].vue:1-13 — the only h3 surface besides the three detail pages, all following one repeated pattern
containment.rationale: Nothing experimental to contain; even the cross-cutting concerns (API base, caching, status codes) are each isolated in one composable or lib module, so any upstream API shift would be a one-file change.

evidence: app/app/pages/pokemon/[name].vue:147-150 — 404 via useRequestEvent + setResponseStatus, the documented stable pattern (createError alternative also stable)
app/app/pages/index.vue:41-55 — URL-driven filter state built with plain ref/computed/watch and router.push; no experimental router or state features
app/nuxt.config.ts:3 — compatibilityDate '2025-07-15' pins behavior deterministically rather than enabling opt-in experiments
justification.rationale: No experimental APIs are used, and the stable choices are each justified; notably it skips available-but-risky options (e.g. h3 v2/Nitro 3, still in beta) that would buy nothing here.

findings.issue: setResponseStatus from h3 v1 will be removed/changed in h3 v2 + Nitro 3 (currently beta/nightly; web-status change event.status or return semantics), so this import is the one spot a future framework upgrade would touch.
findings.suggestion: Acceptable as-is for the current stable stack; when migrating to Nitro 3/h3 v2, replace these four call sites with the then-documented status API (or throw createError({ statusCode: 404 })) — they are already co-located enough that this is cheap.

summary: The app is maximally conservative: it pins the current stable Nuxt 4.6.3 and uses only APIs that have been stable since Nuxt 3 or h3 v1 (useAsyncData, useState, useRuntimeConfig, useHead, useRequestEvent, setResponseStatus). No experimental flags, preview features, or canary APIs appear anywhere in config or source. The only forward-compat exposure is the h3 v1 setResponseStatus pattern used identically in four page components.
